items: 240 V split-phase battery inverter/charger with a generator input
LiFePO4 battery bank sized in kWh
inverter generator able to charge the battery
DC breaker and bus bar for rack batteries
cart: Sun Gold Power (6000W 48V split-phase inverter charger + 2×/4× SG48100P + 160A breaker + bus bar) vs Amazon (Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus + transfer switch/inlet + inverter generator)
why: ChatGPT says the generator must recharge the battery and that 'not every battery system supports this entire sequence,' so the shopper needs a battery plus a generator-charging path and switching, yet it carded only the bare FranklinWH aPower 2 and not its separately sold Generator Module. Whether the set works depends on 240 V split-phase output, the inverter's generator AC-input and charge-current limit matched to the generator's clean output, and the battery kWh. That creates a real choice between a hardwired 48 V inverter with a rack-battery system and a plug-in 120/240 V power station with a transfer switch and a portable generator.
